full_judgment:
9. Mr Shaheed Alam, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant, submits that respondent No. 1 in his deposition admitted that his father and uncle got compensation on 25-10-1960 and, as such, he had knowledge that the suit land was acquired and on facts and in the circumstances of the case, service of notice was not necessary upon him and, as such, the judgment delivered by the High Court Division affirming the judgments of the Courts below is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the suit is barred by limitation having been filed in 1990 and that in his evidence, the respondent as PW 1 admitted that his father and uncle obtained compensation on account of compensation on 25-10-1960 and, as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. Learned Advocate lastly submits that since the suit land was validly acquired respondent No. 1 could have claimed compensation and cannot restrain the appellant by permanent injunction and that without considering these aspects, the High Court Division discharged the Rule affirming the judgments and decrees of the Courts below and, as such, the impugned judgment should be set aside. 

 "Respondent No. 1 in his deposition admitted that his father and uncle got compensation on 25-10-1960 and, as such, he had knowledge that the suit land was acquired and on the facts and in the circumstances of the case, service of notice was not necessary upon him and he filed the suit in 1990 which was barred by limitation.
